question: I'm a BA junior (P-025) with dual Finance and BAT concentrations. I completed 70-208 (Regression Analysis). Can this count toward both the Finance and BAT concentration requirements?

domain_contributions.programs: Finance concentration: quantitative/analytics courses like 70-208 may satisfy a Finance elective. BAT concentration: 70-208 is analytics-focused and may satisfy BAT requirements
domain_contributions.courses: 70-208 (Regression Analysis, 9 units) — quantitative methods course applicable to both Finance and BAT contexts

key_facts: 70-208 is a quantitative methods course relevant to both Finance and Business Analytics & Technologies
CMU double-counting policy: a course generally cannot satisfy requirements in two separate concentrations simultaneously
Whether dual concentrations follow the same double-counting rules as major/minor needs verification
P-025 should verify with their advisor whether 70-208 can be shared between the two concentrations or must be exclusively applied to one
wrong_if_single_domain: Checking Finance requirements alone accepts 70-208. Checking BAT requirements alone also accepts it. The double-counting issue only arises when both concentration requirements are examined together.
common_mistake: Assuming that within a single major, courses can freely satisfy two different concentration requirements; not knowing that double-counting restrictions may apply across concentrations
reasoning_chain: Step 1 (programs, Finance): 70-208 qualifies as Finance quantitative elective
Step 2 (programs, BAT): 70-208 qualifies as BAT analytics course
Step 3 (policies): Double-counting between concentrations → verify policy
Conclusion: Most likely 70-208 can satisfy only one concentration — P-025 needs to clarify with BA program advisors
